 Jemele Hill's Opinion On Ayesha Curry 'Controversy' Divides NBA Fans
 The Spun Follow Andrew Holleran Add to Preferred Sources Mon, November 9, 2026 at 12:00 AM UTC Jemele Hill's Opinion On Ayesha Curry 'Controversy' Divides NBA Fans Ayesha Curry, the longtime wife and partner of NBA star Steph Curry, is set to star in a Christmas romance movie this year.
 The 37-year-old wife of the NBA star has loved acting for a long time. She acted as a child and has pursued multiple acting opportunities in recent years. However, her on-screen appearance is causing some controversy this year, as some believe that the wife of an NBA star shouldn't be kissing another man on screen. 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Former NFL star LeSean McCoy was among those calling out Ayesha Curry for kissing another man, her co-star Matthew Daddario, in "Second Chance Holiday."
 "What we doin'? Is this real?" McCoy said. "Bro, this is crazy. You got one of the greatest players of all time as your husband, and every time—I don't know if it's me, or […] I seen a while ago where she keeps saying how she wants more attention. And how girls throw themselves at him, and she just still wants to feel like she's wanted."
 "Yo, we're getting carried away now, though," McCoy added. "Now you're in a scene kissing a dude? Ain't look like Steph to me. Bro, I ain't married. And I don't want to speak for people that's not married. But I gotta say something: This is crazy. Why you kissing this man like that? Now, she did say it's not real. So if it's not real, then I respect it."
 Jemele Hill, though, is coming to Ayesha Curry's defense.
 Advertisement Advertisement "1) Ayesha Curry wanted to be an actress prior to being married to Steph. She was in commercials as a kid, did an episode of Hannah Montana and appeared in other things as a child actress.
 "2) Hailee Stenfield is Josh Allen's wife. She has a pretty graphic sex scene with Michael B. Jordan in Sinners and I heard not one peep or any pearl clutching (not that there should have been).
 "I find all the conversations about Ayesha Curry to be rooted in a weird sort of misogyny where people get mad at her because she won't just sit down, shut up and have her entire existence wrapped up in her husband. How dare this woman actually try to find some sort of purpose that's unrelated to her being a wife and mother?
 Shame on her."
 1) Ayesha Curry wanted to be an actress prior to being married to Steph. She was in commercials as a kid, did an episode of Hannah Montana and appeared in other things as a child actress. 
2) Hailee Stenfield is Josh Allen's wife. She has a pretty graphic sex scene with Michael… https://t.co/Dgzub05WVg 
 — Jemele Hill (@jemelehill) November 7, 2026 
 Fans appear to be divided on Hill's comments
 While many are rightfully agreeing with Hill, there are still some who disagree.
 Advertisement Advertisement "I don't see anything wrong here but people did joke about Sinners and she's been acting before Allen while the other seemingly been going on a tour of slight shade of her own life, with the subject heavily focused on attention or lack there of," one fan wrote, referencing Josh Allen's wife, Hailee Steinfeld, acting in "Sinners."
 More to explore
 "I think it's having kids that makes it feel different," one fan added on X.
 "No one cares if she has outside interests, she's been doing cook books, has a podcast, etc. You clearly haven't been following the narrative as she has on numerous occasions expressed her interest in being adored by men and now she is seen kissing on other men. So naturally her motivations are going to be questioned," one fan added.
 Years ago, Ayesha Curry appeared on Red Table Talk and went viral for her comments about women throwing themselves at her husband, while the same does not happen to her.
 Advertisement Advertisement "Something that really bothers me and has given me a sense of a little bit of an insecurity is the fact that, yeah, there are all these women throwing themselves," Ayesha Curry said. "But me, the past ten years, I don't have any of that. I have zero — this sounds weird— male attention. And so I begin to internalize it. And I'm like, is something wrong with me?"
 Ayesha Curry, meanwhile, is expecting to pursue more acting roles in 2027.
